slides.texte_overlay:
7 small signals that make
people listen when you speak
Starting with the conclusion. "My recommendation is plan B, here's why." Leading with the point shows clarity, and people pay attention right away.
Using names in conversation. "Good question, Tom." It pulls people in and shows you're fully present, which makes them listen more closely to you.
Pausing before important words. A half-second pause before the key point makes everyone lean in a little. Timing gives your words weight and makes them stick.
Standing or sitting still while you speak. Calm hands, steady feet. Physical stillness makes your words feel more certain and more worth hearing out.
Having something worth saying. I do five minutes a day of history, art or science, and a fresh fact or story makes people actually want to hear me out.
slides.texte_sophia: I do five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. A fresh fact or story makes people actually want to hear me out.

slides.texte_overlay: Listening fully when others talk. People listen to those who listened to them. Give your full attention first, and you'll almost always get it back in return.
Ending with a clear next step. "So I'll send it tonight." Closing with action shows you're someone who gets things done, not just someone who talks.
